finding.claim: SafeListSanitizer#scrub stores per-call tags/attributes on a single @permit_scrubber held by the sanitizer instance, then runs a Ruby-level traversal. A sanitizer instance shared across threads can scrub one request's HTML with another request's allowlist, so a restrictive call can keep tags/attributes it meant to remove when a permissive call runs concurrently. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE (not executed; no Ruby runtime was available).
finding.source: Caller-supplied html and per-call options (tags:/attributes:) on a shared SafeListSanitizer instance, e.g. one created once and reused as in the class docs at sanitizer.rb:281-284. Attacker controls the html of one request; a concurrent request with a different allowlist is the precondition.
finding.sink: fragment.scrub!(@permit_scrubber) at sanitizer.rb:167 using allowlists read per node in scrubbers.rb:84-97 (@tags) and scrubbers.rb:91-93 (@attributes).

finding.guards_checked: Checked: scrub_attribute URI scrubbing (scrubbers.rb:169), SVG local-href removal (scrubbers.rb:175), style CSS scrubbing (scrubbers.rb:128-135), and mglyph/malignmark/noscript removal (scrubbers.rb:142-157). These still apply to any allowlist, so the race can only widen the tag/attribute set, not disable URI or CSS checks. XSS needs the permissive allowlist to contain an otherwise-blocked dangerous element or attribute. Not checked: whether ActionView creates a fresh sanitizer per call (it is outside this repo). If it does, this path is not reachable from the default helpers.
